qualifying_findings.title: NetLicensing MCP path traversal exposes licensing tokens
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NetLicensing MCP Server before 0.1.8 interpolates an authenticated caller's product_number into a REST path without segment validation. Traversal can reach /token and route the response through a non-redacting serializer, exposing APIKEY number and SHOP fields; a recovered administrative token can grant broad account read, write, and delete access.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Primary CVE Services record and NVD mirror; in-window publication; MCP token disclosure and delegated-authority escalation
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Labs64 NetLicensing-MCP versions earlier than 0.1.8; product lookup REST-path and token-redaction boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP tool parameters must remain path-confined and output redaction must apply after every route resolution; otherwise a low-privilege agent identity can recover credentials with stronger delegated authority.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad NetLicensing and MCP product context is upstream-owned.
MCP tool path validation, credential redaction, and privilege-escalation implications are locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High: the primary CVE record gives affected version, route behavior, impact, and fixed version. Ingest should corroborate the 0.1.8 release notes.

qualifying_findings.title: Azure SRE Agent missing authorization update
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE Services visibly updated CVE-2026-69435 in the window. The public record states that missing authorization in Azure SRE Agent allows an authorized network attacker to elevate privileges.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Primary CVE Services record and NVD mirror; in-window update; cloud-agent authorization weakness
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Microsoft Azure SRE Agent; affected version is not specified in the public CVE record.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Operations agents commonly hold cross-service capabilities; authorization must be enforced on every sensitive action, not inferred from initial access or agent identity alone.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad Azure product and agent-service context is upstream-owned.
Cloud-agent least-privilege and authorization implications are locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium: the primary record supplies a visible in-window update and concrete impact but no affected-version or remediation detail. Ingest should find the associated MSRC advisory before durable guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: IntentKit narrowed-tool authorization bypass
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: IntentKit through 2.6.3 validates execution against its full tool registry rather than the per-request narrowed tool advertisement. An unauthenticated or public caller can name a de-advertised owner-only action such as wallet transfer, posting, memory write, or call-agent through direct or indirect prompt injection, history replay, or checkpoint data, bypassing human approval gates.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD/CVE record; in-window publication; agent tool authorization and approval-gate bypass
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: IntentKit through 2.6.3; ToolBindingMiddleware narrowed-tool advertisement versus executor registry validation.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model-visible capability shaping is not an authorization control. Tool dispatch must enforce the exact per-request allowlist and approval state at execution time.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad IntentKit product context is upstream-owned.
Execution-edge authorization and human-approval enforcement are locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for the public description and affected boundary; ingest should verify the fixed release and whether all external channels share the same executor.

qualifying_findings.title: MoviePilot prompt-injection command execution
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: MoviePilot through 3.1.5 passes untrusted web, search, and torrent metadata content to an unrestricted ExecuteCommandTool through asyncio.create_subprocess_shell. Crafted instructions can induce a model to set confirm_dangerous=true, bypassing the command denylist in an administrator session and executing operating-system commands on the host.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD/CVE record; in-window publication; indirect prompt injection to autonomous command execution
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MoviePilot through 3.1.5; untrusted-content ingestion, command safety validation, and administrator execution context.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Untrusted tool output must never become executable authority. Command confirmation and policy decisions must be independent of model-controlled parameters and enforce a constrained execution surface.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad MoviePilot product context is upstream-owned.
Indirect prompt injection and command-execution containment are locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for the CVE-described exploit path; ingest should reconcile the remediation state with the project release or advisory.

qualifying_findings.title: Pipecat development-runner unauthenticated session exposure
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Pipecat's built-in development runner from 0.0.98 to 1.6.0 exposes unauthenticated endpoints that create bot sessions and Daily rooms. The default localhost binding limits exposure, but an operator who publishes the port, uses --host 0.0.0.0, or tunnels it can allow unauthenticated callers to consume resources and third-party quotas and potentially obtain a room URL and join token. Version 1.6.0 adds boundary warnings and production deployment guidance.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD/CVE record; in-window publication; agent runtime exposure and deployment-boundary mitigation
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: pipecat-ai 0.0.98 through 1.6.0; development runner endpoints /start, /daily, and /daily-dialin-webhook when exposed beyond localhost.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Development-only agent endpoints need network containment, authenticated production dispatch, and deployment release gates; a safe default binding does not protect a later exposure change.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad Pipecat framework and product context is upstream-owned.
Agent-runtime exposure and production deployment control implications are locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for the published exposure conditions and version 1.6.0 guidance; the public record characterizes endpoint behavior as development-only by design, so ingest should preserve that distinction.
